sites.rationale: L3 names R376 as one of four ECL3 amber-codon sites tested in full-length GLP-1R. Topology places ECL3 at 375-378; R376 is confirmed extracellular. Python: res(375)=A (residue_before), res(376)=R (residue_after); the ncAA is incorporated AT position 376, equivalent to insert_after_residue=375. Distance from TM6 end (374) is 2 residues, which is below the >=3 threshold; the pipeline should flag this. Confidence is low because ECL3 is a very short loop (4 aa) and proximity to TM6 may constrain a bulky 15-23 aa epitope tag. Full-length GLP-1R bearing a SNAP-tag at the N-terminus and an amber codon at R376 (one of four ECL3 sites tested) was expressed in HEK293T cells; the amber codon was suppressed to incorporate BocK or SphK (unnatural amino acids bearing fluorescent handles) at position 376, demonstrating site-specific modification of the full-length receptor at the extracellular surface.

sources.claim: Thus, we co-transformed HEK293T cells with two plasmids: one encoding GLP-1R containing a SNAP-tag at the N-terminus and an amber codon at one of four ECL3 sites (H374, R376, G377, and T378); the other encoding an orthogonal PylRS/tRNA pair for charging BocK or SphK ( Fig. 1a ).

sites.functional_impact_measured: cAMP-responsive luciferase assay: myc-tagged GLP-1R showed no significant change in GLP-1 potency compared to untagged receptor.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 (same study) explicitly describe a myc-tag inserted immediately downstream of the putative signal peptide of full-length GLP-1R. The signal peptide is residues 1-23 (landmark-confirmed), so the tag goes after residue 23 (P) and before residue 24 (R), the mature N-terminus. Python confirms res(23)=P and res(24)=R. The cAMP assay result in L1 confirms functional surface expression, making this the highest-confidence site. Full-length human GLP-1R with myc-tag inserted immediately downstream of the signal peptide (after residue 23, the last residue of the 23-aa signal peptide) was expressed in cells; the mature receptor carries the myc-tag at its extracellular N-terminus.

sources.claim: Introduction of a myc-tag to the N-terminus of GLP-1R immediately downstream of the putative signal peptide did not significantly affect the potency of GLP-1 at this receptor when assessed using a cAMP-responsive luciferase assay ( Figure 1 ).

literature_notes: N-TERMINAL SITE (rank 1): Supported by nine ledger lines (L1, L2, L3, L6, L7, L8, L11, L12, L13) using myc, SNAP, GFP, FLAG, and HA tags. L1 is chosen as primary because it provides explicit functional validation (cAMP assay). The signal peptide is residues 1-23 per the landmarks; the tag goes after residue 23 (P) and before residue 24 (R), the mature N-terminus. This is the best-evidenced site. ECL3 SITES (ranks 2-4): L3 reports amber-codon ncAA incorporation at four ECL3 positions (H374, R376, G377, T378) in full-length GLP-1R. H374 falls within TM6 (349-374) per the authoritative topology landmarks and is placed in other_positions. R376, G377, and T378 are within ECL3 (375-378) and are reported as sites. However, ECL3 is only 4 residues long; no position within it satisfies the >=3 residues from BOTH TM boundaries constraint simultaneously (R376 is 2 from TM6; G377 is 2 from TM7; T378 is 1 from TM7). The ncAA insertions are also much smaller than a 15-23 aa epitope tag. These sites are reported because the ledger supports them, but confidence is low and the pipeline TM-distance filter will likely exclude them. C-TERMINAL FLAG (L9, L10): The C-terminus of GLP-1R (residues 406-463) is intracellular per the topology; the FLAG tag there is not a surface tag site and is placed in other_positions. ICL3 cpGFP (L4): The cpGFP insertion between K336 and T343 is in ICL3 (intracellular, 326-348); placed in other_positions. L5 confirms the signal peptide is residues 1-23 and supports the N-terminal tag position but does not add a new site. L13 adds FLAG+HA at the N-terminus (same site as L1/L2). L12 adds SNAP-flag at the N-terminus (same site). All redundant N-terminal evidence is noted here rather than creating duplicate sites.
